quick_english: Now the third chapter: if your thought holds action superior, O Janardana, then why do you engage me in terrible action, O Kesava?
cite_parts: athaḥ tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ   jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana
tatkiṃ karmaṇi  ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava

quick_english: You seem to confuse my intelligence with mixed speech; speak one decided way by which I may attain the good.
cite_parts: tatra na dvayoḥ prādhānyaṃ yuktam apitu  jñānasya
tadbalena kṣapaṇīyatvaṃ yadi karmaṇāṃ buddhiyukto  jahātīme ityādinayena mūlata eva tat karmaṇā kiṃ prayojanamiti  praśnābhiprāyaḥ

quick_english: The Lord gives a reply: in this world twofold steadfastness was formerly declared by me, O sinless one.
cite_parts: śrībhagavāṃstūttaraṃ dadāti   loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
sāṃkhyānāṃ jñānaṃ  pradhānaṃ yogināṃ ca karmeti
mayā tu saikaiva niṣṭhoktā  jñānakriyāmayatvātsaṃvittattvasyeti bhāvaḥ

quick_english: A person does not attain inaction by not beginning actions, nor does he attain perfection by renunciation alone.
No one ever stands without acting even for a moment; everyone is made to act helplessly by the gunas born of nature.
cite_parts: jñānaṃ karmaṇā rahitaṃ na bhavati karma ca kauśalopetaṃ  jñānarahitaṃ na bhavati ityekameva vastu jñānakarmaṇī
tathā  coktaṃ   na kriyārahitaṃ jñānaṃ na jñānarahitā kriyā
tasmājjñānāntarvarti karmāparihāryam yataḥ paravaśa eva  kāyavāṅmanasāṃ parispandātmakatvāt avaśyaṃ kiṃcitkaroti

quick_english: He who restrains the action organs yet remembers sense objects by mind is deluded and is called of foolish conduct.
cite_parts: karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran
karmendriyaiścainna karoti avaśyaṃ tarhi manasā karoti

quick_english: One who restrains the senses by mind and begins action-yoga without attachment excels in actions; no knowledge is lost because action proceeds like a machine.
cite_parts: karmasu kriyamāṇeṣu na jñānahāniḥ-manaso'vyāpāre  yantrapuruṣavatkarmaṇaḥ kriyamāṇatvāt

quick_english: Therefore do prescribed action; action is better than inaction, and even body maintenance depends on action.
cite_parts: ataḥ   niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ

quick_english: This world is bound by action other than sacrifice; therefore perform action for sacrifice, free from attachment, since obligatory action without fruit-attachment does not yield binding fruit.

Having created beings with sacrifice, the lord of beings said that through it they should procreate; beings were created together with actions, and actions yield either world-cycle through attachment or liberation through detachment.
cite_parts: uktaṃ ca  tena prajānāṃ karmabhya eva prasavaḥ santānaḥ etānyeva ceṣṭaṃ  saṃsāraṃ mokṣaṃ vā dāsyanti

quick_english: Nourish the gods by this action, and they will nourish you; mutual nourishment of gods and senses quickly yields supreme welfare.
cite_parts: yatra yeṣāṃ mokṣaprādhānyaṃ taireva viṣayāḥ sevyā ityucyate   devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ

tṛptāśca  satyastā vo-yuṣmān ātmana eva svarūpamātrocitāpavargān  bhāvayantu-svātma-sthitiyogyatvāt

quick_english: Gods nourished by sacrifice give desired objects; one who enjoys them without returning is a thief, so enjoyments should be used as they arise.
cite_parts: na kevalamitthamapavarge yāvatsiddhilābhe'pyayaṃ mārga ityāha   iṣṭānkāmānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ

yajñatarpitāni hīndriyāṇi sthitiṃ badhnanti yatra kvāpi  dhyeyādāviti
ata eva tadvyāpāre sati teṣāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ  smṛtisaṃkalpadhyānādinā bhāvāḥ-viṣayā indriyaireva dattāḥ  yadi teṣāmeva upabhogāya na dīyante tarhi stenatvaṃ-cauryaṃ syāt  chadmacāritvāt

quick_english: Those who eat the remainder of sacrifice are freed from all sins, while those who cook only for themselves obtain sin.
cite_parts: bhuñjate te  tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
avaśyakartavyatārūpaśāsanamahimāyātānbhogān ye'śnanti  avāntaravyāpāramātratayā ata eva ca  pṛthagphalatvābhāvāṅgatayā

atha  ca-indriyātmakadevagaṇatarpaṇalakṣaṇayajñāt  avaśiṣṭam-antaḥsārasvātmasthityānandalakṣaṇavighasaṃ  ye'śnanti-tatrārūḍhā bhavanti tadupādeyopāyatayā tu  viṣayabhogaṃ vāñchanti te sarvakilviṣaiḥ-śubhāśubhairmucyante
ye tu ātmakāraṇāditi-avidyāvaśāt sthūlameva viṣayabhogaṃ  paratvena manvānāḥ ātmārthamidaṃ vayaṃ kurmaḥ-iti kurvate

quick_english: Beings arise from food, food from rain, rain from sacrifice, and sacrifice from action.
Know action as born from brahman and brahman from the imperishable; all-pervading brahman is eternally established in sacrifice.
cite_parts: tasmāt  sarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
ityevaṃ suvyavasthito'yaṃ yajñaḥ ṣaḍaraṃ cakraṃ vāhayan  arātrayasandhānādapavargam  arātrayatantraṇādvyavahāramāsūtrayati
iti  vidyāvidyollāsataraṅgasubhagaṃ brahma yajñe eva pratiṣṭhitam
anye tu-annaṃ tāvadvīryalohitakrameṇa bhūtakāraṇam annaṃ ca  vṛṣṭidvāreṇa parjanyāt so'pi yajñāt yajñaḥ kriyātaḥ sā ca  jñānapūrvikā jñānamakṣarāt iti

quick_english: One who does not follow this wheel lives in vain, and one who delights only in the senses is full of sin.
For a human who delights in the self and is self-satisfied, no duty remains.
cite_parts: ātmanyeva ca  santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate

quick_english: For him no purpose arises from action or nonaction, and he acts without dependence on purpose in beings.
cite_parts: ata eva nāsau bhūteṣu kiṃcidātmaprayojanamapekṣya  nigrahānugrahau karoti apitu karaṇīyamidam-ityetāvatā

quick_english: Janaka and others attained perfection through action; seeing world-welfare, you too should act, and they remain examples for those acting toward perfection.
Whatever the best person does, others do; whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
O Partha, I have no duty in the three worlds, nothing unattained to attain, yet I engage in action.
cite_parts: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana

quick_english: If I did not ever act unweariedly, people would follow my path in every way, O Partha.
cite_parts: yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ

quick_english: These worlds would perish if I did not act; I would become maker of confusion and harm these beings.
cite_parts: utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham

quick_english: Therefore, always perform duty unattached; for an unattached person performing action attains the supreme.
As the unwise act attached, the wise should act unattached for the gathering of the world.
cite_parts: prāptaprāpaṇīyasya paripūrṇamanaso'pi karmapravṛttau  lokānugrahaḥ prayojanam-ityatra śrībhagavānātmānameva  dṛṣṭāntamakaroti
karma cet tyajet tallokānāṃ durbheda  evaikaprasiddhapakṣaśithilitāsthābandhatvenāprarūḍhilakṣaṇo  jāyate
yataḥ karmavāsanāṃ ca na moktuṃ śaknuvanti  jñānadhārāṃ ca nāśrayitum

quick_english: The wise should not disturb the intellect of the ignorant, but engage all actions properly.
cite_parts: yataste na samyagjñānena pūtāḥ ato buddherbhedanaṃ-vicālanaṃ  teṣāṃ paramo'nartha ityanugrahāya bhedayenna dhiyameṣām tadāha   na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām

quick_english: The deluded self thinks itself the doer and binds itself falsely.
cite_parts: ajñānamityuktaṃ tadajñatvaṃ darśayati   prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi bhāgaśaḥ

quick_english: Knowing the distinction of strands and action, one does not attach.
cite_parts: guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta  iti matvā na sajjate
guṇakarmavibhāgatattvavittu prakṛtiḥ karoti mama  kimāyātam-ityātmānaṃ mocayati

quick_english: Deluded by nature's strands, people attach to actions; the united should engage in them.
cite_parts: karmasaṅgināmityuktam tat karmasaṅgitvaṃ darśayati   prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu
prakṛtisaṃbandhibhirguṇaiḥ satvādyaiḥ kṛteṣu karmaṣu mūḍhāḥ  sajjanti sattvādiguṇamāhātmyāt

quick_english: Renouncing all actions to me, fight desireless and mineless for world grace.
cite_parts: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi nāhaṃ kartā-iti saṃnyasya svatantraḥ  parameśvara eva sarvakartā nāhaṃ kaścit-iti niścitya  lokānugrahaṃ cikīrṣurlokācāraṃ yuddhātmakamanutiṣṭha

quick_english: Those faithful humans who always practice this teaching are freed from all actions; whoever relies on it and does anything is not bound.
cite_parts: etacca matamāśritya yaḥ kaścidyatkiṃcitkaroti tattasya na bandhakam

quick_english: Those who disparage and do not follow this teaching are deluded and lost; the unfaithful in this knowledge are destroyed continuously because of fear of birth and death.
cite_parts: etasmiṃstu jñāne ye na śraddhālavaste vinaṣṭāḥ-avirataṃ  janmamaraṇādibhayabhāvitatvāt

quick_english: Even the knower acts according to his own nature; beings go to nature and dissolve there, so what can restraint do? Even the knower shows no reversal in conduct such as eating, but acts fittingly; since beings dissolve in nature and the self is non-agent and eternally free, whose birth and so on can be restrained? How then is there bondage? Thus it is said.
cite_parts: prakṛtiṃ  yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
yo'pi ca jñānī na tasya vyavahāre bhojanādau viparyāsaḥ kaścit  apitu so'pi sattvādyucitameva ceṣṭate
evameva jānan yato  bhūtānāṃ-pṛthivyādīnāṃ prakṛtau vilayaḥ ātmā cākartā  nityamuktaḥ iti kasya janmādinigrahaḥ

quick_english: For each sense in its object, attraction and aversion are established; one should not come under their sway, for they are obstacles to him.

One's own duty, though flawed, is better than another's well performed; death in one's own duty is better than another's arising. The world-bound one grasps attraction and aversion toward each object, regarding actions as self-performed through delusion. Even equally in eating and conduct, the knowing and world-bound differ. Our settled doctrine: for one freed from attachment and practicing own duty, no merit-demerit bondage exists, since own duty does not depart from the heart and is rooted in one's own nature; thus no creature is born empty, so it is not to be abandoned.
cite_parts: saṃsārī ca prativiṣayaṃ rāgaṃ dveṣaṃ ca gṛhṇāti
yataḥ  karmāṇi ātmakartṛkāṇyeva vimūḍhatvādabhimanyate iti samamapi  bhojanādivyavahāraṃ kurvatorjñānisaṃsāriṇorastyayaṃ viśeṣaḥ
ayaṃ naḥ siddhāntaḥ-sarvathā muktasaṃgasya svadharmacāriṇo  nāsti kaścitpuṇyapāpātmako bandhaḥ

quick_english: Arjuna asks by what impelled a person commits sin even unwillingly, as if forced, and how a person proceeds knowing it as sin. The question's arising has this intent: if own duty does not depart from the heart, how can unrighteous conduct be this? What is this own duty by which a creature is said to be empty? Here the answer: even though own duty is in the heart, this disturbance is made by a foreign covering, not by its absence.
cite_parts: arjuna uvāca   atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ
pāpaṃ pāpatayā vidannapi janaḥ kathaṃ tatra pravartate ? iti  praśnaḥ

quick_english: Kṛṣṇa says desire and anger, born of rajas, are the great devourer and sin-giver; the wise should know this enemy.
cite_parts: śrībhagavānuvāca   kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ
dvābhyāmetacchabdābhyāmanayoratyantāvaiṣamyaṃ sūcyate etau ca  kāmakrodhau nityasaṃbandhināvanyonyāvinābhāvena vartete  ityekarūpatayaiva vyācaṣṭe
eṣa ca mahasya-   sukhasya aśano-grāsakārakaḥ mahataḥ pāpasya hetutvācca krodha eva  pāpadāyī

quick_english: Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa how this enemy arises, grows, what it is, and what it does.
cite_parts: nanu arthādyupaghātakaṃ jñātasvarūpaṃ ca vastu hātuṃ suśakaṃ  bhavet-ityabhiprāyeṇārjuna uvāca   bhavatyeṣa kathaṃ kṛṣṇa kathaṃ caiva vivardhate
asya cotpattau kiṃ kāraṇaṃ vardhane ca ko hetuḥ svarūpaṃ cāsya  kīdṛk utpannau rūḍhībhūtaśca kimācarati-kiṃ karoti ? iti  praśnāḥ

quick_english: Kṛṣṇa says the enemy is subtle and supreme, deluding Pārtha through the senses, though truly sorrow and delusion.
cite_parts: śrībhagavānuvāca   eṣa sūkṣmaḥ paraḥ śatrurdehināmindriyaiḥ saha
evaṃ ca  vartamānaḥ sukhaṃ tantrayitumivotpadyate vastutastu  duḥkhamohamayaḥ-tāmasatvāt

quick_english: Desire and anger become a terrible ego of pride and joy, hard to cross through sinful actions.
The enemy turns away joy, gives grief, makes fear, and deludes repeatedly; pride grows ego-nature through pleasure-thought.
cite_parts: ata eva ca garvādvardhate'bhimānasvabhāvaḥ sukhabuddhiprakāreṇa  ca jāyate iti trayaḥ praśnāḥ parihṛtāḥ

quick_english: The enemy is impure, fault-seeking, rajas-driven delusion that destroys this and other worlds by faults.
cite_parts: sa eṣa iti cchidrāṇi prekṣate-amunā cchidreṇāsyehalokaparalokau  nāśayāmi-iti
arjuna uvāca   yatkrodhano yajate yaddadāti yadvā tapastapyate yajjuhoti
vaivasvatastaddharate'sya sarvaṃ moghaḥ śramo bhavati krodhanasya

quick_english: Just as fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so this self is covered by that. Through these three examples are said its hard-to-remove quality, its doing of forbidden acts, and its being a seat of disgust: this is the self.
Knowledge is covered by desire, the knower's eternal enemy, O Kaunteya—an insatiable fire that roams through the senses and burns both seen and unseen, never to be filled.

quick_english: Thus, having known what is beyond intellect and steadied oneself by oneself, slay the enemy, mighty-armed, formed of desire and hard to approach. The senses are other than sense-objects marked as enemy; mind is other than them; intellect is distinct even from mind; and the self is that whose nature is other. How can anger born of the senses agitate mind, intellect, or self? Thus consider. The intent of secret knowers is that intellect abides elsewhere; supreme ego is all-I identity-nature, supreme nonduality. Because the full has no fragmentation, anger and the rest do not arise. Therefore, grasping supreme ego—other-enthusiasm, consciousness-natured anger, ignorance-natured enemy—slay it; auspicious.
